title: Which read gets the next free worker
impact: Moonshot: rejected on incidence, not mechanism. Exp 265 measured a point read behind four 1,000-row reads at 533-1169 us against 37-52 us inline (claim 265.2) and named that the admission half of the round-trip price; exps 265, 269 and 270 each tried to collect it by removing the worker and were rejected for unbounded caller work, unbounded opaque SQLite work, and foreign-writer staleness. `ReaderPool._dispatch` never scheduled it at all — first free worker, one FIFO park queue, and nothing in the path knowing that one parked request returns a row in 8 us and the one ahead of it ten thousand in a millisecond. The cost signal exp 239's rejection demanded (`a reliable private cost signal`) has existed since exps 260/264 built `RowSizeMemory.highWater` for buffer sizing, one line above the worker scan. Two arms, three AOT binaries, two collections of order-flipped lane-isolated pairs. Priority waiter queues alone move eight point reads queued behind eight large ones -37 to -42% with every control neutral and the starvation guard reproducibly FASTER (-3 to -9%), because serving short jobs first empties the queue sooner. Adding a last-free-worker reservation — safe without any per-request denial cap because a slot is only ever refused while another worker is busy, so a wake is always still coming — takes a point read into a saturated pool from 256-374 us to 52-65 us (-75 to -86%, against ~20 us on an idle pool), which is most of exp 265's inline win with no SQLite on the calling isolate, no staleness contract and no starvation. Both are rejected. A temporary counter over one full release-suite pass found 335,221 dispatches, 325,909 of them cheap, 312 cheap reads that parked at all, and ZERO parked behind a costly waiter — the entire population the reordering acts on, measured with the reservation ON so the zero is an upper bound. The reservation additionally costs a reproduced +47 to +63% on four concurrent large reads whenever cheap reads are recent, which is the same hidden latency-for-throughput trade exps 197, 213, 239 and 249 were each rejected for. Also corrects exp 265's `point-under-load` lane: sticky dispatch (exp 266) puts reads two through ten on an already-free worker, so summing ten reads diluted this candidate to -13%. Runtime reverted, prototype with 162 passing tests at `archive/exp-275`, harness retained. The bound to carry forward is that a four-worker pool parks a cheap read three times in a thousand across every workload the repo can run.
